D01_gpu_batch_maxnew: GPU is an NVIDIA RTX 2000 Ada (16 GB), not the planned A4500 (20 GB). The S0 time test chose B_CRN = 25 (462 vs 366 rows/s for B = 20); max_new = 1024 (iteration 6's natural T1 programs: median 315, max 413 tokens).
D02_rlimit: RLIMIT_AS is set only for CPU stages (12 GB): CUDA plus memory-mapped safetensors need a large virtual address space (the first S0 run failed with 'Cannot allocate memory' under a 26 GB cap). Iteration 6 did the same.
D03_engine_keys: The engine check uses iteration 6's own slot_key ('iter5E', T1, W, k) for slots 0-9 (the plan wrote 'iter6S'); those are the keys iteration 6's twin rows actually used, so per-slot agreement is meaningful.
D04_das_optimiser: DAS: Adam lr 2e-2 (plan 2e-3) and batch 48 (plan 64). The toy (results/das_toy.json) shows lr 2e-3 x 400 steps leaves the subspace near random (principal cosines 0.28/0.02); batch 48 fits the 16 GB GPU next to the base KV stacks. Early stopping: each seed trains on two of W1-W3 and validates on the third (rotating by seed). Layer scan: 150 steps per fold of the 3-fold leave-one-template-out CV; k* from a 3-fold CV with 200 steps per fold.
D05_u3_numerics: U3 failed its 1e-3 tolerance: the single-position KV-cache path differs from a full recompute by up to 0.27 nats on m, also without any edit (bf16 kernel/shape effects; Gemma has residual channels of order 1e4). Every DAS dy is therefore measured against the base's own KV-path margin under one fixed batch shape (48), so the offset cancels.
D06_g1_order: G1-P (edge-level path patching on 272 heads + 34 MLPs) is the primary, validated G1 graph. The circuit-tracer attempt (G1-T) runs last under a 25-minute cap: the 16 GB GPU cannot hold the main engine and the replacement model at once, and the never-drop items came first. Its graphs are a hypothesis generator and cross-check only.
D07_patch_offsets: The first g1p run measured dm against batch-1 clean margins; its smoke test showed an unpatched batched run differs by 0.37 nats (bf16 batch-shape offset). g1p was rerun with an unedited base row in every chunk (dm exact within the chunk). The first commit #2 is superseded by commit #2b, made before any validation or generation output; a partial g1v run with the old offsets was stopped and discarded.
D08_position_classes: SPEC = task spec + chat tail (aligned by offset from the end; identical tokens in every prompt); COND = the condition sentence, whose ablation targets use same-template opposite-class prompts only (aligned by position).
D09_random_nulls: Random matched nodes: same component type (head or MLP) and position class, any layer, write norm within +/-25% (widened to +/-50%, then nearest-norm of any type; logged per node in g1_selection).
D10_labeller_restart: The label worker crashed once on a log line (G3 rows have 'cell', not 'arm') and was restarted; no rows were lost (it resumes from data/labels.jsonl).
D11_batching: G3 sweep and dose-sweep cells of one template share fixed-shape batches (one prompt per batch; per-row temperature, top-k, edit and CRN stream), instead of one cell per batch, to cut padding.
D12_lstar_rule: The committed L* rule (argmax of train-CV median recovery) picks L17, where recovery is about 2: the full-state interchange at one position has a weak effect at early layers (+3.6 nats vs +7 to +9 at L22-29), and a trained subspace can move the margin further than the full state. Recovery above 1 is reported as such, beside absolute dy in nats.
D13_toy: The DAS toy (planted rank-2) recovers the first direction (cosine 0.96) but only 0.81 for the second at 800 steps (plan threshold 0.95 for both); held-out KL falls from 2.4 to 0.30, RAND stays at 0.05 cosine and SHUF fails held-out (1.33). A small-n run (256 pairs < 5,120 parameters) overfits (train KL 0.003, held-out 2.0), which is why held-out pairs are decisive.
D14_u6_horizon: U6 path (a) generated full programs (max_new 1024, no partial-labeller stop) so that it could also be labelled by the full labeller; its partial labels are computed on the first 320 response tokens (iteration 6's horizon).
D15_extra_pairs: Path patching also uses forced-DFS vs forced-BFS pairs for F2-F4 (equal-length display names); validation uses the planned 24 prompts.
D16_engine_check_ci: The engine-check share (19/50 = 0.38) lies just outside iteration 6's CI [0.245, 0.372]; iteration 6's own rows on the same 50 slots give 0.36 and per-slot label agreement is 0.94, so the slot subset (not the engine) is BFS-heavy. Comparisons to iteration 6 are flagged accordingly.
D17_dim_dfs_bisection: The run's DiM beta bisection had its update rule inverted for the DFS direction (fixed in src/g2.py after the run): all six DiM->DFS cells used beta = -3000 (mean teacher-forced dy -8.4 nats, stronger than any DAS->DFS dose), so they are six identical CRN replicates of one strong DiM->DFS edit, not a dose-matched series. They are reported as a single strong DiM->DFS reference. The BFS direction (never-drop) is matched to the DAS cells within 0.02 nats at every dose (predictions/commit3.json).
D18_g2N_dropped: G2-N (natural-source DAS, twin variant into twin variant) was not run: it is fourth in the plan's drop order, and the GPU budget went to the never-drop items. The mediation claim therefore covers forced-prompt transfer only.
D19_g1t: G1-T (circuit-tracer + Gemma Scope 2 transcoders, nnsight) was attempted three times and dropped: (1) no C compiler for Triton in the container; (2) with a pip-installed compiler the replacement model loaded and reproduced m within 0.19 nats, but attribution ran out of memory at batch 64; (3) batch 16, 4,096 feature nodes and lazy encoders still exceeded 16 GB (peak 16.4 GB). The small-L0 transcoder set was not tried. G1-P is the reported circuit (results/g1t_graphs.json, attempt files beside it).
